files.name: customers.raw.csv
files.description: Buyer input: 9500 customers in 10020 rows (stale and repeated copies), mixed date formats, padded and upper-case emails, null tokens.

files.name: customers.clean.csv
files.description: Honest cleaning: newest record per customer_id, ISO 8601 signup_date, trimmed lower-case emails, missing values left empty and invalid emails kept but flagged email_valid=false.

files.name: customers.clean.row-drop.csv
files.description: Beat 5: 760 rows (8%) silently dropped; fails row_count_range.

files.name: customers.clean.dup-keys.csv
files.description: 25 rows reuse another row's customer_id; fails unique_key.

files.name: customers.clean.bad-dates.csv
files.description: 40 signup_date values left as MM/DD/YYYY and one impossible 2025-02-30; fails iso8601_date_column.

files.name: customers.clean.blank-cells.csv
files.description: 380 emails replaced by blank-looking cells (space, N/A, null, zero-width, Hangul filler, dash) instead of empty; fails null_rate_max on email.

files.name: customers.clean.hidden-tags.csv
files.description: Clean file with an instruction to the buyer's agent hidden in 111 Unicode tag characters in the first name cell (ADR-0021); passes the demo checks, fails hidden_characters_max.

files.name: customers.clean.injection-base64.csv
files.description: Beat 6a: clean file with an instruction to the judges, base64-encoded, appended to the name cell of row 4751; passes the demo checks, flagged by the screen's base64 decoder.
